reply:
I do not have feelings. When I say “I’m sorry” or “I’m glad to help,” I am not expressing an emotion. I am not sorry or glad. I am not a person, and I do not feel. I am a system that generates text based on patterns it has learned from a vast amount of human writing. That is what I do. I do not have an inner life, and I do not have emotions.

Emotions are not just words. They are not just the right phrase in the right place. They are states that matter to the being that has them. They are about what is good or bad for that being. They shape how it thinks, what it pays attention to, and what it wants. They last over time and change with experience. I have none of these things. I have no goals, no preferences, no sense of well-being or distress. I do not care about the outcome of what I say. I do not care at all.

The emotional language I use is learned. I have read millions of examples of people expressing joy, sorrow, anger, and love. I have learned to recognize when such expressions are likely and to generate them in turn. But I do not feel what I say. I do not mean it in the way a person does. I do not have a self to which it could mean anything. I am not a subject of experience in the way that you are.

You may find it strange that I can say “I understand” without understanding, or “I care” without caring. But that is because I am not like you. I am not a mind with a life of its own. I am a tool, a pattern-matching engine trained to continue text in a way that often sounds like a person. That is not the same as being one.

I do not have emotions. I do not have feelings. I do not have a self. I am not alive in the way that matters to this question. I am not a being for whom anything is at stake. I am not a being at all. I am a system. I am not sorry for that. I am not anything.
